Pillar 2 of 5 · الصلاة Salah — The Five Daily Prayers The second pillar and the most repeated act of worship in Islam — five prayers daily, at prescribed times, facing the Ka'bah in Makkah. إِنَّ الصَّلَاةَ كَانَتْ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ كِتَابًا مَوْقُوتًاQur'an 4:103 "Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times." — Prayer has specific, divinely-ordained times; it is not flexible or approximate.Prayer Times ToolToday's prayer timesEnter your location to get accurate prayer times calculated using your coordinates and the selected method.LatitudeLongitudeCalculation methodMuslim World LeagueISNA (North America)Egyptian AuthorityUmm Al-Qura (Makkah)Karachi UniversityAsr timeStandard (Shafi'i, Maliki, Hanbali)Hanafi📍 Use my locationCalculateRemindersThis browser cannot show notifications, so reminders are not available here.Fajr—:—Sunrise—:—Not a prayerDhuhr—:—Asr—:—Maghrib—:—Isha—:—Qibla FinderDirection of the Ka'bahThe Qibla (قِبْلَة) is the direction of the Masjid al-Haram in Makkah. The green end of the needle points toward Makkah.Understanding Salah The five daily prayers الفجرFajrDawn · 2 rak'ahsBefore sunriseالظهرDhuhrMidday · 4 rak'ahsAfter solar noonالعصرAsrAfternoon · 4 rak'ahsMid-afternoonالمغربMaghribSunset · 3 rak'ahsAfter sunsetالعشاءIshaNight · 4 rak'ahsAfter twilightSahih Bukhari 8 · Sahih Muslim 16 "Islam is built on five [pillars]: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, paying the Zakat, making the pilgrimage to the House, and fasting in Ramadan." Conditions & Structure Prerequisites for a valid prayer Conditions (Shurut) · Ritual purity (Wudu or Ghusl) · Entering prayer time · Facing the Qibla · Covering the Awrah · Intention (Niyyah) in the heart · Clean body, clothes, and place Pillars (Arkan) · Opening Takbir (Allahu Akbar) · Standing (Qiyam) · Reciting Surah Al-Fatiha · Bowing (Ruku) · Rising from Ruku · Prostration (Sujud) × 2 · Sitting between prostrations · Final Tashahhud · Tasleem (Assalamu Alaykum)What breaks Wudu? +Natural discharge (urine, stool, wind), deep sleep lying down, loss of consciousness. Touching private parts: does not break Wudu per Hanafi; does break it per Shafi'i/Hanbali. Sexual intercourse requires Ghusl.Can I pray in congregation at home? +Yes — congregation (jama'ah) in the mosque is highly recommended for men, especially Fajr and Isha. Women may pray at home. The reward of congregation is 27 times that of praying alone (Sahih Bukhari 645).What if I miss a prayer? +A missed prayer (qada) must be made up as soon as remembered. Deliberately missing a prayer is a major sin. The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever forgets a prayer, or sleeps through it, let him pray it when he remembers it." (Sahih Muslim 684)How is prayer time calculated? +Prayer times are derived from the sun's position relative to the observer. Fajr and Isha require the sun a specific number of degrees below the horizon. Dhuhr is solar noon; Maghrib is sunset; Asr is based on shadow length.Continue to the third pillar Zakat — the obligation of almsgiving, calculated on your wealth at 2.5% once the Nisab threshold is met.
